narration.full_text: The human brain is the main coordinating center of our body. It's broadly divided into three major parts: the Fore-brain, the Mid-brain, and the Hind-brain. Let's start by understanding the Fore-brain. The Fore-brain is considered the most complex and specialized part of the brain. It primarily consists of a large structure known as the cerebrum. The cerebrum is responsible for many of our higher-level functions. For instance, it's the thinking part of the brain, allowing us to process information and make decisions. It also controls all our voluntary actions, like walking or writing. The Fore-brain is also where we store information, acting as our memory center. Furthermore, it receives sensory impulses from various parts of the body, integrating them to give us a complete perception of our surroundings. Finally, it houses centers associated with basic needs like hunger.
